result.markdown: --- title: "Session 4 — Shrinkage and Variable Selection" subtitle: "Stepwise selection and its instability · ridge · lasso · uniform shrinkage · Lab 4" author: "Community Medicine Workshop" format: revealjs: theme: serif css: [../assets/slide_deck.css, assets/workshop.css, assets/quiz.css] include-after-body: assets/quiz-include.html embed-resources: true slide-number: true navigation-mode: linear code-copy: true center: false transition: fade width: 1280 height: 720 fig-align: center html-math-method: plain execute: echo: true warning: false message: false fig-width: 9 fig-height: 4.6 fig-dpi: 100 --- ## Where we are ::: {.incremental} - Session 3: the all-markers model is **overfitted** (bootstrap slope 0.80) - Today: ways to **reduce overfitting** - **variable selection**: does it work? - **penalised regression** (ridge, lasso) - **uniform shrinkage** ::: # Topic 1 — Variable selection {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Backward stepwise (AIC) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} m_step <- step(m_all, direction = "backward", trace = 0) names(coef(m_step))[-1] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "age" "waist" "fam_history" "hypertension" "activity" [6] "smoker" "m6" "m8" "m9" "m10" ``` ::: ::: ::: {.warn} The selection kept **age, waist, family history, hypertension, activity, smoking** (BMI and sex were dropped) **and four noise markers: m6, m8, m9, m10**. With 84 events, selection **chases chance**. ::: ## How stable is the selection? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(3) sel <- replicate(50, { i <- sample(nrow(dev), replace = TRUE); f <- suppressWarnings(step(glm(f_all, data = dev[i, ], family = binomial), direction = "backward", trace = 0)); paste0("m", 1:10) %in% names(coef(f)) }) round(setNames(rowMeans(sel), paste0("m", 1:10)), 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` m1 m2 m3 m4 m5 m6 m7 m8 m9 m10 0.46 0.18 0.24 0.24 0.12 0.56 0.16 0.50 0.70 0.82 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - **Bootstrap inclusion frequency**: every noise marker is selected **12% to 82%** of the time (m10 82%, m9 70%) - The chosen set **changes with the sample**; **coefficients of selected variables are biased away from zero**; **p-values after selection are not valid** - **Do not** select by univariable p-values either - Prefer: **pre-specify** predictors (clinical knowledge, literature), **penalise**, or accept **shrinkage** ::: # Topic 2 — Penalised regression {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Ridge ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(1) cv_r <- cv.glmnet(x_all, y, family = "binomial", alpha = 0) round(cbind(ML = coef(m_all)[paste0("m", 1:10)], ridge = as.numeric(coef(cv_r, s = "lambda.min"))[-1][match(paste0("m", 1:10), colnames(x_all))]), 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` ML ridge m1 -0.160 -0.095 m2 0.013 0.012 m3 -0.055 -0.038 m4 0.065 0.044 m5 0.037 0.011 m6 0.217 0.136 m7 0.027 0.018 m8 -0.205 -0.145 m9 -0.236 -0.158 m10 0.266 0.170 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - **Ridge** adds a **penalty on the size of the coefficients** (λ × sum of squares) - **λ is chosen by cross-validation** (`cv.glmnet`; here λ = 0.036) - All coefficients **shrink towards zero** (to about **60 to 70%** of the ML values), **none becomes exactly zero** - **Standardise** the predictors (glmnet does it by default) ::: ## Lasso ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(1) cv_l <- cv.glmnet(x_all, y, family = "binomial", alpha = 1) b_l <- coef(cv_l, s = "lambda.1se") rownames(b_l)[as.numeric(b_l) != 0][-1] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "age" "waist" "fam_history" ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} The **lasso** (penalty on the **sum of absolute values**) sets some coefficients **exactly to zero**: it **selects and shrinks**. At **λ.1se** (largest penalty within one SE of the best) it kept **only age, waist and family history**: it removed all the **noise markers**, but also the real **hypertension, smoking and activity**: a sparse, probably **over-shrunk** model. `lambda.min` keeps more. ::: ## Uniform shrinkage ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} lp0 <- predict(m_all, dev) lp_s <- 0.80 * lp0 b0 <- coef(glm(diabetes ~ offset(lp_s), data = dev, family = binomial))[[1]] c(mean_predicted_after = mean(plogis(lp_s + b0)), prevalence = mean(dev$diabetes)) |> round(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` mean_predicted_after prevalence 0.12 0.12 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - Multiply **all coefficients** by the **bootstrap slope (0.80)**, then **re-estimate the intercept** so that the mean risk equals the prevalence - Predicted risks become **less extreme**; the **ranking (AUC) does not change** - Simple, transparent, and works with **any** model; the same idea as **ridge**, with one factor ::: ## What to use? ::: {.good} 1. **Pre-specify** a small set of predictors; avoid data-driven selection when events are few 2. If you must reduce, use **penalisation** (ridge for prediction; lasso for sparse models) 3. Always **bootstrap the whole process** (including λ selection and selection steps) 4. Apply **shrinkage** when the bootstrap slope is below about 0.9 5. **External validation** (Session 5) tells you whether it worked ::: ## 🔧 Switch to R — Lab 4 {.lab-slide background-color="#1565c0"} ::: {.lab-box} **File:** `prediction-workshop/labs/lab4_shrink.R` - stepwise selection and its bootstrap stability - ridge and lasso with `cv.glmnet` - uniform shrinkage ::: **Time:** 40 minutes · answer the Q questions in the comments ## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="p4q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="sfkvg8.jjumvq" data-show="U2VsZWN0aW9uIGZvbGxvd3MgY2hhbmNlIGluIHNtYWxsIHNhbXBsZXMsIGFuZCB0aGUgc2V0 IHZhcmllcyBieSBzYW1wbGU=" data-explain="V2l0aCBmZXcgZXZlbnRzIHBlciB2YXJpYWJsZSwgc2VsZWN0aW9uIGZvbGxvd3MgcmFuZG9t IHBhdHRlcm5zLCBhbmQgZGlmZmVyZW50IHNhbXBsZXMgZ2l2ZSBkaWZmZXJlbnQgbW9kZWxz LCBhcyB0aGUgYm9vdHN0cmFwIGluY2x1c2lvbiBmcmVxdWVuY2llcyBzaG93Lg=="} Backward stepwise selection kept four noise markers. What is the main lesson? - The markers are real predictors that were missing from the study design plan - Stepwise selection removes noise variables, but it fails with the real ones - Selection follows chance in small samples, and the set varies by sample - Backward selection works if forward selection has been applied first ::: ## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="p4q2" data-type="mcq" data-hash="sfl8oy.jjv1d4" data-show="SXQgc2hyaW5rcyBhbGwgY29lZmZpY2llbnRzIHRvd2FyZHMgemVybyB3aXRob3V0IHNldHRp bmcgdGhlbSBleGFjdGx5IHRvIHplcm8=" data-explain="VGhlIHJpZGdlIHBlbmFsdHkgaXMgb24gdGhlIHNxdWFyZXMgb2YgdGhlIGNvZWZmaWNpZW50 cywgc28gYWxsIG9mIHRoZW0gYXJlIHB1bGxlZCB0b3dhcmRzIHplcm8gYnkgYW4gYW1vdW50 IHRoYXQgZGVwZW5kcyBvbiBsYW1iZGEu"} What does ridge regression do to the coefficients? - It sets small coefficients to exactly zero and keeps the large ones unchanged - It increases the largest coefficients to improve discrimination - It removes correlated predictors from the model before fitting - It shrinks all coefficients towards zero without setting them exactly to zero ::: ## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="p4q3" data-type="mcq" data-hash="sfllxk.jjvfue" data-show="QnkgY3Jvc3MtdmFsaWRhdGlvbiwgdGFraW5nIHRoZSB2YWx1ZSB3aXRoIHRoZSBiZXN0IG91 dC1vZi1zYW1wbGUgZml0" data-explain="Y3YuZ2xtbmV0IGZpdHMgdGhlIHBlbmFsaXNlZCBtb2RlbCBvdmVyIGEgZ3JpZCBvZiBsYW1i ZGEgdmFsdWVzIGFuZCBldmFsdWF0ZXMgZWFjaCBieSBjcm9zcy12YWxpZGF0aW9uLiBUaGUg YXBwYXJlbnQgQVVDIHdvdWxkIGZhdm91ciBubyBwZW5hbHR5IGF0IGFsbC4="} How is the penalty lambda usually chosen in glmnet? - By cross-validation, taking the value with the best out-of-sample fit - By the analyst, who picks the value that gives the best apparent AUC value - By the p-value of each coefficient in the unpenalised version of the model - It is fixed at the value 1 for all datasets and need not be chosen at all ::: ## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="p4q4" data-type="mcq" data-hash="sflz6a.jjvubs" data-show="SXQgY2FuIHJlbW92ZSBub2lzZSwgYnV0IGFsc28gcmVhbCBwcmVkaWN0b3JzIHdoZW4gdGhl IHBlbmFsdHkgaXMgbGFyZ2U=" data-explain="QSBzdHJvbmcgcGVuYWx0eSBzZXRzIG1hbnkgY29lZmZpY2llbnRzIHRvIHplcm8sIGluY2x1 ZGluZyByZWFsIG9uZXMuIENob29zaW5nIGxhbWJkYS5taW4gb3IgY2hlY2tpbmcgZXh0ZXJu YWwgY2FsaWJyYXRpb24gc2hvd3Mgd2hldGhlciB0aGUgbW9kZWwgaXMgb3Zlci1zaHJ1bmsu "} The lasso at lambda.1se kept only age, waist and family history. What does this illustrate? - Those three are the variables that are really related to diabetes in the data - It can remove noise, but also real predictors when the penalty is large - The lasso keeps variables in the order of their p-values in the full model - Variables with a low prevalence cannot be selected by the lasso procedure ::: ## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="p4q5" data-type="mcq" data-hash="sfmcf1.jjw8t7" data-show="TXVsdGlwbHlpbmcgY29lZmZpY2llbnRzIGJ5IGEgZmFjdG9yIGJlbG93IDEgYW5kIHJlZml0 dGluZyB0aGUgaW50ZXJjZXB0" data-explain="QSBzaW5nbGUgZmFjdG9yLCBvZnRlbiB0aGUgYm9vdHN0cmFwIGNhbGlicmF0aW9uIHNsb3Bl LCBwdWxscyBhbGwgY29lZmZpY2llbnRzIHRvd2FyZHMgemVyby4gVGhlIGludGVyY2VwdCBp cyByZWZpdHRlZCBzbyB0aGF0IHRoZSBhdmVyYWdlIHJpc2sgc3RheXMgY29ycmVjdC4="} What is uniform shrinkage? - Dividing the dataset into equal parts and fitting a separate model in each - Setting every coefficient to the average of the coefficients of the model - Rounding all coefficients to the nearest whole number for use as a score - Multiplying coefficients by a factor below 1 and refitting the intercept ::: ## Score and take-home **Your score: ** ::: {.incremental} - **Stepwise** selection is **unstable**: noise markers chosen, biased coefficients - **Ridge** shrinks all; **lasso** shrinks and selects - **λ by cross-validation**; standardise predictors - **Uniform shrinkage** = bootstrap slope × coefficients, new intercept - Pre-specify predictors; **validate externally** ::: **Next:** Session 5: external validation, decision curves and reporting

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
